notes: The original scan is 1691 by 2362 pixels. The whole original was viewed once for layout, and both supplied native-resolution halves were viewed once and read line by line against C and H.

Eight crops were made from original coordinates and visually inspected: opening [300,25,1675,380], cutting-sides [300,370,1681,598], normalisation-map [300,625,1625,929], stability [300,928,1675,1455], supposed-curve [300,1455,1663,1817], association-ending [300,2040,1658,2248], final-map [300,2207,1667,2351], and folio99 [25,2295,100,2348]. Each filename is crops/147_scan100_<name>.png. No rotation was applied. Crops used autocontrast, LANCZOS enlargement to width 2800 (folio99: 2200), and mild UnsharpMask radius 1, percent 80, threshold 3.
The sheet starts with lowercase la as a continuation. No missing beginning is supplied. The repeated live les les is retained even though awkward. H's intervening arêtes ou is not on this leaf.

The opening parenthesis ends marqués.) with the period inside. The first displayed map has no terminal period. The stability parenthesis has the written comma after its final G and closes after aussi without a period. These punctuation features are preserved.

The source underlines découpe and strict once. H's emphasis wrappers can represent those underlines and are not treated as independent errors. By contrast, the actual raised double quotation marks around découpe, coupant and enlever differ from H's guillemets.

The author describes a découpe of G following C by cutting the middles of the edges in C; the parenthesis says this amounts to removing edges and replacing the corresponding sides by marked points. This is a report of the written description, not a verification of the construction.

The author states that for a strict normalisation morphism G-prime to G, G-prime is stable if and only if G is stable; the following parenthesis states a surjectivity condition on the written S-prime/S connection and a stability implication. These claims were transcribed, not independently proved or used as a proof certificate.

The final paragraph states that a special curve X over a base S, pinned by G, receives an associated special curve bearing the locally ambiguous C-prime/G-prime description, followed by the written functor M_G(S) to M_{G-prime}(S). The displayed target index is clear G-prime. This local context does not erase the actual uncertainty of the earlier open letter.

The bottom formula number is visibly overworked, but its last digit cannot be separated into a demonstrated deleted numeral and a demonstrated replacement. The transcription therefore retains the local 0/1 doubt without inventing cancellation/insertion chronology. H's note about overwriting is editorial apparatus, not additional manuscript text.
No hyphen is visible before épinglée. The uncertainty between C and G concerns the letter only; the prime is clear and the intervening space is clear.

H appends qui pour S variable ... sont stables after the final display. This entire paragraph is absent on scan 100, whose lower edge follows the displayed map and comma. Its location elsewhere was not investigated.
Manuscript page 49 is written at the top. Pale foliation 99 appears separately at the lower-left edge. The pale writing is recorded without assigning its hand to a named person.

There are two displayed single maps and no additional diagram or drawing on this leaf. Both shafts, source/target expressions, primes, indices, labels, and the final comma are included. There are two cancellations and no independently demonstrated insertion. The live Si following the cancelled opening is baseline text.

The six local uncertainties are documented in doubts and applicable mark decisions. Certainty-only refinements of m's stop, the connector subtype, C/G, or the final numeral are excluded from substantive C/H correction counts. M1143 is resolved on its crop without counting C's matching candidate as an error.

The blind second-reading boxes combine adjacent regions so their readings include every written element within the boundaries. They cover all three assigned marks, both cancellations, all C/H differing words, both full displayed formulas, the doubtful inline formula, the four written numeral groups 49, 130, 13[0/1], and 99, and every below-high-confidence departure from C. No TeX compilation or external research was performed.

Main-reader cross-page layout check: the corresponding continuation beginning qui pour S variable is physically written at the head of scan101, which the main reader viewed independently. Thus H has assigned that continuation to the end of scan100. Its exact wording is collated on scan101; the absence on scan100 is a page-placement finding, not a claim that the entire passage was invented.

Blind audit retains the first reading after every token difference is checked: authorial 49, la découpe, obtained ending obtenue, repeated live les les, côtés, m with doubtful stop, cancelled raised prime, the one-sided connector uncertainty, literal comma after G, tentative cancelled Supp., C/G and the altered final numeral. Alternative math/display wrappers carry no reading change.
